niche: a Spanish home-workout subscription app placing each paid acquisition channel of its 2027 media plan in the growth policy's scale, hold or cut band, on the 12-month net revenue per euro that the plan's weekly spend on the channel buys
answer: Scale Snapchat iOS and Pinterest iOS, hold Meta iOS, TikTok iOS, Google iOS, Google Android and AppLovin Android for 2027 (return per euro at the plan's weekly spend, generator/core.py: Snapchat iOS 1.329, Pinterest iOS 1.329; Google iOS 1.089, Meta iOS 1.071, Google Android 1.033, AppLovin Android 0.992, TikTok iOS 0.988); three decisive steps on three axes, each with a figure of its own (AppLovin Android 50.4 and Meta iOS 47.5 monthly-plan payments per 100 installs, 233,300 installs the plan buys), the first step alone moving five of the seven bands
answer_source: task1/generator/figures.json, written by the generator from the cut pack; task1/submission.md
analyst_test: A careful but hurried analyst takes the billing records as they stand, prices each network's unnamed installs with the payer and revenue gap read off the labelled channels and carries the plan at full delivery; that route files scale for Meta iOS (1.740) and Google iOS (1.270) and cut for AppLovin Android (0.766), three of the seven bands wrong, and lands the other four only because its errors offset (no answer line whole).
domain_test: Each result is an acquisition-economics and lifetime-value quantity of a subscription app (what an install went on to pay in twelve months where the app's records stop at the last open, what a network's installs are worth where the attribution export names no channel, what a weekly budget buys in an auction, the return per euro at a plan's spend and what the next euro returns); swap the nouns for another field's and the store reports, the tracking prompt, the install postbacks, the campaign flights and the ad auction stop making sense.

world.org_type: a home-workout and yoga subscription app

driver: Each unit's band rests on what a year of its planned outlay returns, a quantity no record holds: the detailed record takes in a payment only when the payer is next seen and the payers no longer seen go on at a rate of their own, which only the complete summary's excess over the detailed record shows period by period; the units no record ties to a source sit in one pool whose outcome is known only as a whole, and because each source steers what it takes in blind by an early signal it still receives, the gap the labelled sources show is wrong on every other, so one fraction per source is fitted together from how the pool's outcome moves as each source's known count in it moves; and the planned outlay is what a supplier will bill of a set amount, so what it buys is read on the amount set, with the share delivered beside it.
driver_concrete: Zancada's growth policy places a paid channel in scale, hold or cut on its 12-month net revenue per euro at the 2027 plan's weekly spend (1.20 and 0.90 the lines). A store charge reaches the billing records only at the subscriber's next open and a store subscription nobody opens is rarely cancelled (0.97 a month, against 0.71 on the web checkout, which emails a receipt for every charge), so the records miss 1 per cent of Meta iOS's twelve-month revenue and 36 per cent of AppLovin Android's. On iOS the export names a network's install only where the user allowed tracking (27 per cent); the rest sit among the accounts with no channel, worth 0.45 (Meta) to 0.72 (Google) of the named ones, and because a network still gets each install's first-48-hour value in its postback and steers its blind buys by it, the payer and revenue gap the labelled channels show is wrong on every network. And the plan's weekly figures are billed spend, what the platform delivered of a budget (83 to 87 per cent over the 104 weeks), so the plan's spend needs its budget.
stump: Both responses on record took the billing records as they stand (S1), which cuts TikTok iOS, Google Android and AppLovin Android and holds Snapchat iOS and Pinterest iOS against the golden's bands; Response 1 also priced each network's unnamed installs with the payer and revenue gap borrowed from the labelled channels (S2), which scales Meta iOS (1.47) because an iOS network steers what it buys blind by the first-48-hour value its postbacks return; Response 2 priced the plan at full delivery (S3), which puts the plan's installs 15.5 per cent high and alone scales Meta iOS, Google iOS and Google Android. Each step dropped alone flips its own channel, none fixed alone reaches the call, and a run careful on S2 and S3 still files five bands wrong.
results: R1 the monthly-plan payments per 100 installs that each Android channel's installs of the year to 2 November 2025 made in their first twelve months; R2 the same for each iOS network, over every install it bought; R3 the installs the whole 2027 plan's billed spend buys; R4 the twelve-month net revenue those installs bring; R5 each channel's 2027 return per euro at the plan's weekly spend; R6 each channel's band
